core.title: Name each DESIRED OUTCOME with a unique step-coded URN matching the profile-declared DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape
core.given: Any artifact (plan artifact, product capability manifest, acceptance, doc or source), by any author, contains a DESIRED OUTCOME (what-must-be-true) URN.
core.when: A DESIRED OUTCOME URN is created, modified or referenced.
core.then: The URN is a unique identifier conforming to the DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape declared by the profile (urn.desired-outcome) — its product capability segment is the parent product capability's id in the shape's casing, its step code is a single letter from the shape's step-code vocabulary, and its sequence is zero-padded within the shape's range — and it is built with the stack's canonical DESIRED OUTCOME URN builder (urn.builder#artifact).
prefer: Generate the URN with the stack's canonical DESIRED OUTCOME URN builder rather than hand-typing it.
Use the parent product capability's own id, in the casing the URN shape declares, as the product capability segment.
Pick the step letter from the shape's step-code vocabulary and a zero-padded sequence within the shape's range that keeps the URN unique.
avoid: Reusing a URN already assigned to another DESIRED OUTCOME (URNs must be unique).
Unpadded or out-of-range sequences, or step codes that are not a single letter of the shape's step-code vocabulary.
Using a product capability segment that is not the parent product capability's id or does not follow the shape's casing rule.
core.why: The DESIRED OUTCOME URN is the DESIRED OUTCOME's stable identity: it embeds the owning product capability and step code so file names, acceptances and traceability tooling can resolve it unambiguously.
evidence: Every DESIRED OUTCOME URN matches the DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape declared by the profile (pattern and sequence range).
The product capability segment equals the id of the product capability that contains the DESIRED OUTCOME.
No two DESIRED OUTCOMES share the same URN.
verification: Scope: any artifact of any kind and any author that contains a DESIRED OUTCOME URN; the trigger is the URN content, not the artifact kind or the author.

A check validates every DESIRED OUTCOME URN against the profile-declared DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape (urn.desired-outcome): pattern, capability-segment casing, step-code vocabulary and sequence range; a sequence that matches the pattern but falls outside the range is still invalid. It also checks that the product capability segment equals the id of the containing product capability and that no two DESIRED OUTCOMES share a URN.

Detecting that a DESIRED OUTCOME URN was created, modified or referenced in any artifact requires a diff-level observer for candidate DESIRED OUTCOME URNs — strings carrying the scheme of the profile-declared DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape (urn.desired-outcome), including malformed ones — not only strings already matching the full valid shape; the full shape and sequence-range validation applies after activation. Without such an observer this change-based activation is not observable (marked needs_new_observer).

Not covered: URNs of other artifact kinds (e.g. product capability, feature, acceptance, component), and edits to a DESIRED OUTCOME's statement or acceptances that neither create, change nor reference its URN.

fires: A new DESIRED OUTCOME is added to a product capability and given its URN
A DESIRED OUTCOME is renamed, renumbered or moved to another product capability or step
An acceptance, doc or code file writes a reference to a DESIRED OUTCOME by URN
Code or tooling mints a DESIRED OUTCOME URN programmatically
doesNotFire: Edits to a DESIRED OUTCOME's statement or acceptances that neither create, change nor reference a DESIRED OUTCOME URN
URNs of other kinds (product capability, feature, acceptance, component) being authored

profileRequirements.meaning: The DESIRED OUTCOME URN shape this rule enforces: full pattern, capability-segment casing, step-code vocabulary and sequence range (a sequence can match the pattern yet still be out of range), plus the scheme used to detect candidate DESIRED OUTCOME URNs — including malformed ones — before full validation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: ^desired-outcome:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[DLPCEMYRK][0-9]{3}$; sequence_range: 001-999 (000 is invalid even though it matches [0-9]{3}); product capability segment kebab-case ([a-z][a-z0-9-]*); step codes D, L, P, C, E, M, Y, R, K; candidate detection: any string matching desired outcome:* (malformed candidates included), validated against the full shape after activation

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's canonical construct that builds a DESIRED OUTCOME URN from the product capability id and sequence, which the core prefers over hand-typing the string.
The concrete plan-artifact kinds that can contain a DESIRED OUTCOME URN and trigger this rule; the neutral activation speaks of plan artifacts and the profile names the stack's kinds.
profileRequirements.bunValue: desired outcome, product capability manifest, plan doc

bunOnly.text: Term desired_outcome_urn = the DESIRED OUTCOME identifier; validate with regex ^desired-outcome:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[DLPCEMYRK][0-9]{3}$.
bunOnly.reason: The verifier term id of this realization's check is a rule-local identifier; the core's verification names the check generically and the concrete pattern is carried by profile key urn.desired-outcome.

bunOnly.text: Valid examples from source: desired-outcome:resolve-dilemmas:E001, desired-outcome:burn-timebank:M045, desired-outcome:user-mgmt:C023.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete instance URNs of this repository's product capabilities; the neutral core points at the profile-declared shape and the reference rewrite is delivered as the worked example.

bunOnly.text: Concrete invalid sequences (e.g. 1, 45, 000, 1000) and multi-letter / lowercase step codes.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete anti-examples of the reference realization; the core keeps the role-level negation and does not repeat concrete examples.

classification.note: Already role-level: any artifact kind, any author; 'plan doc'/'source code' restated as plan artifact/source.
Neutral as-is: a DESIRED OUTCOME URN is created, modified or referenced.

The concrete form, kebab-case product capability segment, step letters and 001-999 range become the urn.desired-outcome profile value; the concrete builder becomes urn.builder#artifact; the core keeps uniqueness, parent-capability binding and shape conformance.

Step-code vocabulary (D, L, P, C, E, M, Y, R, K) and 001-999 range come from the declared shape.
Uniqueness negation is already neutral.
Neutral negation in the core; the concrete invalid sequences stay as realization examples.
Non-parent-capability negation is core; the concrete casing violations (uppercase, underscores, leading digit) are the shape's kebab-case rule.
The concrete regex and range are the urn.desired-outcome value; the core cites the declared shape.
Neutral: product capability segment equals the containing product capability's id.
Neutral uniqueness evidence.
Term id is realization-only; the regex is the urn.desired-outcome value; 'validate each URN against the shape' becomes a generic verification entry.
The 001-999 range is shape data; the subtlety that a pattern-matching sequence can still be out of range is kept generically in verification.
The canonical builder is profile idiom data referenced by the core obligation.

Kind names neutralized to plan artifact/source; the concrete plan-side kinds (desired outcome, product capability manifest, plan doc) are the profile value. Trigger is URN content, not artifact type.
Task terms are neutral planner vocabulary and stay in core activation.

Change values are neutral; the diff-level observer must catch candidate DESIRED OUTCOME URNs (malformed included) before full shape and range validation, so malformed URNs cannot escape activation; the concrete candidate-detection scheme is carried by the urn.desired-outcome profile value; the observer requirement is folded into verification.

neutralityNotes: The concrete URN grammar (the desired outcome: scheme, kebab-case product capability segment, step-code vocabulary D/L/P/C/E/M/Y/R/K, three-digit zero-padded 001-999 sequence) is carried by profile key urn.desired-outcome rather than spelled out in the core, following the vocabulary's design that URN shapes are profile data; the same key supplies the candidate-detection scheme (in its concrete profile value, any string carrying the desired outcome: scheme), so the diff-level observer activates on malformed candidate URNs and full shape and range validation is applied after activation; instantiated with that profile value plus the bunOnly items the core imposes exactly the source obligation. The canonical builder (URNBuilder.desiredOutcome(capability_id, sequence)) has no existing vocabulary key and is proposed as urn.builder#artifact while also being listed in profileRequirements. The rule declares no severity or disposition, so the core's verification states scope and coverage only. The verifier term id (desired_outcome_urn) and the concrete example URNs stay in the realization; 'product capability', 'DESIRED OUTCOME' and the step codes are planner-structure vocabulary, not stack machinery, so they may appear in the core.
